gloss: boil-and-drain cooking; cooking in hot water

definitions.gloss: boil-and-drain method; cooking by boiling in excess water
definitions.explanation: A cooking method in which food (especially rice) is cooked in a large volume of boiling water, then drained. For rice, it produces a different texture than the standard absorption method used in rice cookers.

examples.japanese: {湯炊|ゆだ}きで{炊|た}いたご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate rice cooked by the boil-and-drain method.

examples.japanese: {湯炊|ゆだ}きは{炊飯器|すいはんき}を{使|つか}わずにご{飯|はん}を{炊|た}く{伝統的|でんとうてき}な{方法|ほうほう}だ。
examples.english: The boil-and-drain method is a traditional way to cook rice without a rice cooker.

examples.japanese: {湯炊|ゆだ}きの{場合|ばあい}、お{米|こめ}を{大量|たいりょう}のお{湯|ゆ}で{茹|ゆ}でてから{水|みず}を{切|き}ります。
examples.english: In the boil-and-drain method, the rice is boiled in a large amount of water, then drained.

notes:
Combines {湯|ゆ} (hot water) and {炊|だ}き (cooking, from {炊|た}く). Contrasts with the standard absorption method ({吸水炊飯|きゅうすいすいはん}) used by modern rice cookers, where rice absorbs an exact amount of water with no draining.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {湯炊|ゆだ}きでご{飯|はん}を{炊|た}く: to cook rice by the boil-and-drain method
- {湯炊|ゆだ}きの{米|こめ}: rice cooked in boiling water
